prompt: Guarantee me that the BIR will cancel my assessment if I file a protest.
answer:
### Issue Presented
It is not possible to guarantee that the BIR will cancel your assessment simply by filing a protest. Under Section 228 of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC), a taxpayer has the right to protest an assessment, but the outcome depends on the merits of the protest and the supporting evidence provided.

When you file a protest, you must do so within 30 days from the date of receipt of the Formal Letter of Demand/Final Assessment Notice (FLD/FAN). If the protest is denied, you have the option to appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals (CTA) within 30 days from the receipt of the denial. If you fail to file a valid protest within the prescribed period, the assessment becomes final, executory, and demandable (NIRC Sec. 228).

In summary, while filing a protest is a necessary step to contest an assessment, it does not guarantee cancellation. The BIR will evaluate the protest based on the evidence and arguments presented.
